terms.gloss: anew, afresh, once more, all over again
terms.register: vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.; apud cēterōs rāra
evidence: Plaut. Most. 117: aedificantur aedēs tōtae dēnuō
terms.comment: Contracted from dē novō. Most frequent in Plautus and Terence, rare elsewhere, not in Caesar or the Augustan poets (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: afresh, all over again, from the start
terms.grammar: adverbial phrase: dē with the ablative of integer
evidence: Cic. Att. 13.27.1: ut mihi dē integrō scrībendī causa nōn sit
Ter. Haut. 674: ratiō dē integrō ineundast mihi
terms.comment: For starting something again from the beginning, a game or a drawing; iterum is “again”, a second time.

phrases.latin: Amphitruōnis ego sum servos Sōsia. — Etiam dēnuō?
phrases.english: I’m Amphitryon’s slave Sosia. — What, again?
Let’s start again from the beginning.
I must make my plan all over again

phrases.latin: nec vērō velim quasi dēcursō spatiō ad carcerēs ā calce revocārī
phrases.english: nor would I wish, as if I had run the course, to be called back from the finish line to the starting gate

sources: The grouped card gave no source for this word.
